errors.evidence_quote: We assume opposite faces of a cube are the same color: Red ↔ White, Green ↔ Yellow, Blue ↔ Purple
errors.description: The model incorrectly assumed a fixed pairing of opposite faces (e.g., Red ↔ White) without any visual or textual evidence in the video to support this. The ground truth explicitly shows each cube has six distinct colors assigned independently to each face, with no such symmetry. This false premise led to systematically incorrect assignments of hidden face colors and ultimately an incorrect final answer.

errors.description: The model made an unsupported assumption about which faces were visible and which were hidden based on a generic 3D cube orientation, rather than relying on the actual visual configuration shown in the video. The ground truth specifies the exact visible/hidden faces (IN, OUT, LEFT, RIGHT, UP, DOWN) for each cube, which the model ignored in favor of a speculative default orientation.

analysis_result.analysis: The model failed due to two critical reasoning errors: (1) fabricating a false premise about opposite-face color pairing that contradicts the actual cube configuration, and (2) speculatively assuming a standard cube orientation instead of using the explicit face visibility data provided in the scene. These errors snowballed into an incorrect color count, leading to the wrong answer 'purple' instead of the correct 'yellow'. The model’s logic was internally consistent but grounded in invalid assumptions not supported by the visual evidence.
